title: Compare full BIOS boot and fast boot after a PS2 startup error
summary: Run paired cold launches with the same BIOS, image, and card to see whether a startup fault changes when the normal firmware sequence is skipped.
heroAlt: Several PlayStation 2 console models shown side by side.
author: EmuCore - Hub

blocks.text: PCSX2 exposes fast-boot and slow-boot launch options. Fast boot skips the normal firmware startup sequence; a full BIOS boot lets the PS2 firmware run first. Comparing them can narrow a startup problem, but cannot repair a damaged game image or replace a valid BIOS. Use firmware dumped from your own console and game images made from discs you own, following applicable law.

Pick a title that has booted before and keep the emulator build, BIOS, disc image, graphics settings, and memory-card assignment fixed for both trials. Shut down completely between runs. A save state is unsuitable because it resumes an earlier machine state and bypasses startup. Record the last screen seen and whether sound or a logo appeared.

items: 1. Confirm the selected BIOS and image path; do not download firmware or game data for this check.
2. Cold-boot through the normal full BIOS path and record the sequence and error point.
3. Close emulation fully and launch the same image with fast boot enabled using the emulator’s supported setting.
4. Compare the last visible screen and time to failure while leaving all other settings unchanged.
5. If only fast boot fails, repeat the full BIOS path and inspect firmware setup or title-specific compatibility notes.
6. If both fail at the same point, verify your personal dump and recorded checksum before changing graphics options.

blocks.text: A difference between the two cold boots is evidence that the skipped firmware path or a title’s startup assumptions matter. The same failure in both modes points toward the image, region, emulator, or game compatibility. Record the BIOS identifier, game serial, emulator version, and symptom; neither result alone proves the exact cause.

items: Fast boot reaches the logo then hangs: reproduce with full BIOS before blaming the renderer.
BIOS asks for clock or language: change only that firmware preference, then repeat a cold boot.
The game appears to have lost a save: confirm the same card and port are assigned; cancel any format prompt.
The image hash differs from your record: stop using the changed copy and verify the untouched source.

blocks.text: Return the launch option to its recorded value, remove any temporary command-line flag, then cold-boot once with the normal configuration. Keep the original disc image unchanged; if its verification fails, make and check a new personal dump before retiring the old copy.
